curation.lead:
Alba Fiber Systems Inc is a domestic business corporation incorporated in New York on 2012-04-23 (NY DOS ID 4234896), initially registered in Queens County and relocated to Nassau County (Valley Stream) in June 2013 [Finding #711]. The company manufactured industrial fiber optic transmission equipment — switches, media converters, and video/audio/data transmission hardware — and operated from Suite 209 at 265 East Merrick Road, Valley Stream, NY 11580 [Finding #711]. Its IEEE OUI registration (block 50:A0:BF, assigned May 2, 2013) demonstrates that the company was a genuine hardware manufacturer, not a shell entity: the IEEE's MA-L block assignment requires demonstrable hardware production [Finding #753]. Products were distributed through Anixter, a major industrial distributor, and archived website snapshots from 2013–2017 confirm an active product catalog during that period [Finding #753]. The company's website (albafiber.net) had expired DNS as of February 2026, and no SEC, 990, or federal court filings were found [Finding #711].

Alba Fiber entered the Epstein investigation via a Bureau van Dijk corporate-data phone pivot: the company appeared in a dataset alongside nine confirmed Epstein entities — including SLK Designs, JSC Interiors, Zorro Management, and Birch Tree BR LLC — when pivoting on the phone number (212) 971-1307 [Finding #712]. Investigators conducted an exhaustive review across more than 20 data sources, including the full DOJ Vol 11 corpus (331,000+ pages), DugganUSA (204,000 documents), LMSBAND (60,000 files), and the Unified DB (70,000 documents), and returned zero results for "Alba Fiber," "albafiber," or "Perry Behr" [Finding #712]. Alba Fiber's own registered phone numbers (516-837-9449, 516-218-2541, 516-218-2542) do not match any known Epstein-network number [Finding #712]. The word "Alba" does appear three times in the DOJ Vol 11 email corpus, but those references are to "Project Alba" — a codename for an HBOS bank acquisition Epstein was evaluating in September 2009 — and bear no connection to the Valley Stream company [Finding #713].

Based on this review, investigators concluded that the BvD phone pivot was a data-quality artifact, most likely caused by phone-number reassignment or database aggregation error [Finding #755]. Perry Behr, the individual associated with Alba Fiber on LinkedIn, held the title of Regional Sales Manager (not owner or officer) and had prior roles in security and surveillance sales; he appears in none of the Epstein document corpora and holds no listed officer position in the New York Secretary of State records [Finding #752]. The building at 265 East Merrick Road is a multi-tenant commercial property housing multiple logistics and customs-brokerage firms; no Epstein-network entities have been placed at that address [Finding #754]. The investigation's final assessment treats Alba Fiber as an unrelated entity that was erroneously co-clustered with Epstein corporate data by a third-party aggregator [Finding #755].
curation.system_role: Alba Fiber Systems Inc was a small Long Island industrial hardware manufacturer that entered the Epstein investigation solely through a data-aggregation artifact in Bureau van Dijk's corporate phone records. Exhaustive multi-source review found no substantive connection to the Epstein network.

sections.title: Corporate Identity and Operations
sections.content:
Alba Fiber Systems Inc was incorporated in New York on April 23, 2012, as a domestic business corporation (NY DOS ID 4234896), initially in Queens County [Finding #711]. A Certificate of Change filed on June 17, 2013, relocated its registered county to Nassau [Finding #711]. The company's address of record was Suite 209, 265 East Merrick Road, Valley Stream, NY 11580 — an 11,760 sq ft multi-tenant commercial building assessed at roughly $1.16 million that also housed logistics and customs brokers including Cargo Control Inc, Concordia International Forwarding Corp, Quality Custom Brokers, and Consolidated Transport Service [Finding #754]. The company's product line included industrial ethernet switches (model AFS8202M), media converters, and video/audio/data transmission hardware, distributed through Anixter [Finding #753].

The IEEE registered MAC address block 50:A0:BF to Alba Fiber Systems Inc on May 2, 2013 — an MA-L (Large) block allocating roughly 16 million addresses, a class of assignment that requires demonstrable hardware manufacturing activity [Finding #753]. The AFS8202M product line bears resemblance to the ROBOfiber HGW-808S, which investigators assessed as consistent with an OEM or rebrand relationship rather than original design [Finding #753]. Wayback Machine archives captured more than 50 snapshots of the company website between 2013 and 2017, confirming normal commercial operations during that window [Finding #711]. The domain albafiber.net had expired DNS as of February 2026, consistent with a company that ceased active operations [Finding #753].

The individual associated with the company in external records is Perry Behr, who held the title of Regional Sales Manager at Alba Fiber Systems — not listed as an officer or owner in the New York Secretary of State records for any company [Finding #752]. Behr's documented career history includes Regional Sales Manager roles at Genetec Inc (a Canadian video surveillance and access control platform), Security Engineers Inc, and Structure Works Inc [Finding #752]. No results for Perry Behr appear in any of the Epstein document corpora searched, in SEC EDGAR, or in OCCRP Aleph [Finding #752].

sections.title: The Bureau van Dijk Phone Pivot
sections.content:
Alba Fiber entered the Epstein investigation when a Bureau van Dijk corporate-registry pivot on the phone number (212) 971-1307 returned it alongside nine entities with documented connections to Jeffrey Epstein: SLK Designs, JSC Interiors, Zorro Management, Zorro Development, Neptune LLC, Neptune Industries, Neptune Partners, Neptune Corp, and Birch Tree BR LLC [Finding #712]. Alba Fiber's own phone numbers — 516-837-9449, 516-218-2541, and 516-218-2542 — do not appear in any Epstein-related records, and (212) 971-1307 was not registered to Alba Fiber in any primary source reviewed [Finding #712].

Investigators searched the full DOJ Vol 11 corpus (331,000+ pages), DugganUSA (204,000 documents), LMSBAND (60,000 files), and the Unified DB (70,000 documents) for "Alba Fiber," "albafiber," and "Perry Behr" and returned zero results across all searches [Finding #712]. An additional Dehashed phone-number search placed Alba Fiber at 265 East Merrick Road but again produced no documentary link to Epstein-network entities; investigators assessed that connection as a probable false positive given the frequency of errors and reassignments in breach-database phone records [Finding #721].

The word "Alba" does appear three times in the DOJ Vol 11 email corpus — documents EFTA02436485, EFTA02436641, and EFTA02436791 — but refers exclusively to "Project Alba," a codename used in September 2009 for an HBOS bank acquisition under evaluation [Finding #713]. Those emails also reference "Oppenheim," "Ports" (assessed as likely DP World), and "Michelin House, Fulham Road" in London; they have no lexical or contextual connection to the Valley Stream company [Finding #713].

sections.title: 265 East Merrick Road: Address Context
sections.content:
The building at 265 East Merrick Road, Valley Stream, NY 11580 is a multi-tenant commercial office property built in 1985, assessed at approximately $1.16 million [Finding #754]. It functions as a logistics and customs-industry cluster: tenants documented during the period of interest include Cargo Control Inc, Concordia International Forwarding Corp, Quality Custom Brokers, Consolidated Transport Service, Atlantis Business Solutions, Care Network Services LLC, and the accounting firm Krinsky & Epstein PC [Finding #754]. The accounting firm — whose principals are Lee S. Epstein CPA and Philip J. Krinsky CPA — is unrelated to Jeffrey Epstein [Finding #754].

7 Seas Supply Chain Management Corp (NY DOS 4404512) occupies Suite 208 — the suite immediately adjacent to Alba Fiber's Suite 209 [Finding #750]. 7 Seas was incorporated on May 16, 2013, by CEO Hector F. Grajales, and operates as a freight forwarder with offices in New York, Los Angeles, Hong Kong (contact: Bennie Chu), Shanghai, Guangzhou, Qingdao, Vietnam, Indonesia, and Colombia [Finding #750]. It holds FMCSA USDOT 3531779 and MC-1176016, carried BBB accreditation from 2017, and reported approximately $7 million in revenue with 37 employees [Finding #750]. No evidence links 7 Seas SCM to Perry Behr or to Alba Fiber: the principals are different, the business types are different, and the incorporation dates are independent [Finding #750]. The co-location is consistent with the building's role as a general logistics hub [Finding #754].

sections.title: Investigative Assessment
sections.content:
After reviewing more than 20 data sources — including DOJ Vol 11, DugganUSA, LMSBAND, the Unified DB, SEC EDGAR, OCCRP Aleph, FL SunBiz, FEC, FARA, CourtListener, LittleSis, ProPublica 990, FMCSA, IEEE OUI registry, BBB, and ImportYeti — investigators reached a confirmed assessment: the BvD phone pivot that placed Alba Fiber alongside confirmed Epstein entities is a data-quality error, most likely caused by phone-number reassignment or aggregation error in Bureau van Dijk's corporate records [Finding #755]. The five evidentiary pillars supporting this conclusion are: (1) Alba Fiber's own phone numbers do not match any Epstein-network number; (2) Perry Behr has no documented presence in any Epstein corpus; (3) the company holds a legitimate IEEE OUI block requiring hardware manufacturing; (4) zero corpus hits across 660,000+ Epstein documents; and (5) no import-record or financial connection to Epstein's Asia Gateway or David Stern network was identified [Finding #755].

Alba Fiber Systems Inc is assessed as unrelated to the Epstein network. It was a small, legitimate industrial hardware company operating in Valley Stream, Long Island, that ceased active web presence by approximately 2017 and ceased operations by an undetermined date before February 2026 [Finding #711, Finding #753]. The investigation is closed on this entity absent new primary-source evidence.

open_questions: What is the ownership structure of Alba Fiber Systems Inc? NY SoS filings list no officers; the identity of the principal(s) behind NY DOS ID 4234896 remains undocumented.

When did Alba Fiber cease operations, and under what circumstances? The website went dead between 2017 (last Wayback snapshot) and February 2026, but no dissolution filing or corporate status change has been confirmed in the NY SoS record.

Does the product-line resemblance between the AFS8202M switch and the ROBOfiber HGW-808S reflect an OEM supply relationship, and if so, who was the upstream manufacturer? The OEM source may have been a Chinese hardware vendor, but no import records were located via ImportYeti.

What mechanism caused the Bureau van Dijk record to associate Alba Fiber's address with the Epstein-network phone number (212) 971-1307? Identifying the specific aggregation pathway would clarify whether other BvD-sourced phone pivots in this investigation carry the same artifact risk.

Is Perry Behr's current whereabouts and employment status known? His last documented role was Regional Sales Manager at Alba Fiber; no subsequent employment or corporate registration has been identified in available records.
